title: auth-api-401-429-debug-scratchpad-ashley-2026-03-28
content:
Goal:
Quick notes + breadcrumbs while debugging the 401/429 spikes observed by a handful of clients (today, 2026-03-28). This is my scratchpad — messy, chronological.

Symptoms observed:
- Multiple customer reports: intermittent 401s and 429s for same API key over ~2hr window (09:20–11:45 PDT).
- Errors observed in client logs: 401 Unauthorized {"error":"invalid_api_key"} and 429 Too Many Requests {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded"}.
- Some customers see 401s then 429s, others only 429s.
- No single region outage in Grafana during the window; overall API success rate dip ~0.8% (spike correlates with ~09:20).

What I reproduced locally:
- Replayed a subset of example requests with the same API key via curl (from my laptop, us-west1).
- Hit both 401 and 200 depending on small change: when I include header exactly as "Authorization: Bearer abcdef" -> 200. When header has trailing quotes or env var rendered with quotes ("Authorization: Bearer "abcdef"") -> 401.

Example commands and outputs I ran:
- curl good:
  curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXX" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'
  HTTP/2 200
  x-request-id: req_...

- curl bad (missing space):
  curl -i -H "Authorization:Bearer sk-live-XXXX" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  HTTP/2 401
  {"error":"invalid_api_key"}

- curl bad (quotes in env var):
  export RW_KEY="sk-live-XXXX"
  curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  HTTP/2 401

- Reproduced 429 via burst test (simulated client):
  for i in {1..120}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}
" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-THROTTLE" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings & done
  Observed many 200s then a block of 429s. Response headers contain: "Retry-After: 10", "X-RateLimit-Limit: 60", "X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0"

Initial hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
1) Client-side formatting errors: env var quoting, missing space after "Bearer" — explains intermittent 401s where some requests were correct and some not (scripts sometimes inject quoted values).
2) Key rotation/invalidation: possibility that key rotated during window. But console shows no recent key rotation for affected keys (checked via Keys UI).
3) Upstream caching/proxy inconsistent strip/modify Authorization header (e.g., some edge proxies strip Authorization for preflight or when certain headers present) -> would cause sporadic 401s. Need to check ingress logs for header presence.
4) Rate limiter config change or bug triggered for specific customer traffic shape -> 429s. Could be new autoscaling policy causing throttle when concurrency spikes.
5) Shared-key collisions: multiple services using same key and exceeding per-minute quotas.

Checks I performed so far:
- Console (Admin -> API keys): verified key status for a few affected customers -> all show active, last-used timestamps align with reported window.
- Billing/limits page for sample customers: no billing suspension.
- Ingested logs: grep for "invalid_api_key" in prod-ingress logs between 2026-03-28T09:00 and 2026-03-28T12:00 -> ~140 hits; majority from customer A and customer B .
- Traced a few request ids from customer A: matched to edge instance edge-az1-12; checked Nginx access log -> Authorization header present in access log for the 401 requests. This reduces probability of header being stripped at edge.
- Checked edge -> auth service logs: auth-service returned 401 with code "invalid_token_format" for some requests (see snippets below).

Auth-service snippets (sanitized):
- 2026-03-28T09:22:17Z auth-service WARN request=req_abc id=... reason="token parse failed: unexpected '\"'"
- 2026-03-28T10:01:02Z auth-service INFO request=req_def id=... key_id=sk_123

Rate-limit snippets:
- 2026-03-28T09:34:40Z rate-limiter WARN req=req_xyz key=sk_123 bucket=per_minute remaining=0 -> 429, Retry-After=15
- X-RateLimit headers emitted from gateway: X-RateLimit-Limit: 120, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0

Notes / tentative conclusion so far:
- 401s: Mixed cause. A chunk is definitely caused by malformed tokens (quotes/missing space). Evidence: auth-service parse errors referencing unexpected '\"'. Also reproduced locally with quoted env var. BUT some 401s have correct Authorization formatting in access logs; these map to auth-service decisions: possible key invalidation mid-window or auth-service cache inconsistency between replicas. Need to check key cache invalidation events (redis cache flushes / key sync).
- 429s: Expected behavior when a single key exceeds per-minute quotas. For customers that saw both 401 and 429, pattern could be: some requests malformed -> 401 counted differently? Unclear. Another pattern: bursty client spawns many concurrent connections which push usage over limit and then subsequent requests are 429.

Next actions (todo):
- Ask SRE to check Redis/key-cache churn around 2026-03-28T09:00-11:50. Look for cache flush events, crash/restart of auth-service replicas (auth-service-1/2/3).
- Instrumented replay: rerun customer A's request trace (sanitized) against staging with auth-service-replicas toggled to reproduce parse error.
- Add additional logging at gateway to log raw Authorization header (masked) for one-minute window for affected keys. Must coordinate with privacy policy (mask token).
- Check rate-limiter config change history: PRs merged last 48 hrs (search in git) — tag Samir since he touched limiter.
- Reach out to customer A and B for request samples (curl-ready) and exact SDK version.

Quick checklist for customer-facing response (short):
- Acknowledge: we see intermittent 401/429s; investigating.
- Ask for: exact timestamp, request id(s), sample request/headers and SDK version.

Appendix: quick reproductions/snippets for future pasting
- env var quoting issue:
  $ export RW_KEY="sk-live-abc"
  $ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health -I
  HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  # fix:
  $ export RW_KEY=sk-live-abc
  $ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health -I
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK

- missing space issue:
  bad: -H "Authorization:Bearer $RW_KEY" -> 401
  good: -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" -> 200

- bursting simulation for rate-limiter:
  for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} " -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-burst" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings & done

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight and update as SRE/auth/limiter findings come in. If we confirm cache invalidation bug, escalate to oncall and patch release for auth-service (low-risk fix: retry key fetch on parse error + better logging).

End of scratchpad (ashley)
